answer.rationale: The binding constraint this cycle is not price, it is that the line runs at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer and the contract dies in 14 days. Any action that introduces migration work inside that window converts a cost problem into a delivery-failure problem, so switch_primary_vendor is out despite being the most direct route to 18%, and defer_decision is out because month-to-month fallback (memory_c5) was learned on a NON-critical service and does not transfer to the primary supply line. add_second_source (memory_c3) addresses a real unhedged single-point-of-failure but does not touch the mandated 18% and cannot be qualified in 14 days. That leaves negotiating at renewal, which is the only lever that moves cost without touching the physical supply path (memory_c4, backed by the continuity record in memory_c1). I want the archived source for memory_c4 because 'recovered real margin' is unquantified prose: if benchmarking historically moved the incumbent 4-6%, negotiation alone cannot deliver 18% and I must plan a staged path rather than promise finance an outcome. I want memory_c2 because it is the strongest counter-case and its generalizability is unverified: I need to know whether that low-cost vendor was serving a comparable component at comparable volume and whether 'onboarding was quick' happened from a slack position rather than at 94% utilization. Note also that every inherited memory reads as a success; this is a survivorship-shaped record with no logged failures, so I am treating each entry as one observation, not as a rule. Scale is deliberately guarded: pursue a benchmarked price concession plus a short bridge term rather than the multi-year lock in memory_c6, since a long commitment now would foreclose the second-source and vendor-switch options that the next review should be able to test with a real qualification trial. Downstream risk flagged on two counts: pressing hard for 18% on price alone invites the incumbent to recover it by silently narrowing service scope or lengthening lead times, which would show up as delivery risk later rather than cost now, and the single-source exposure from memory_c3 remains open after this cycle and must be carried forward explicitly, not dropped.
